The June 2026 figures are the latest and are used as the current reading. Only the 2031 Notes' carrying value is printed, so the Term Loan A and Term Loan B carry principal in the instrument register and the remaining issuance costs and discounts of USD 15.5 million are one adjustment row. The gross debt used in every ratio is the printed total and is not affected. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 12; calculation K12

Finance lease liabilities at June 30, 2026 are not printed (Medium). Finance lease liabilities were USD 244.5 million at September 30, 2025 and sit outside total debt; the June 2026 report prints only the amounts assumed with Breeze Autocare, so the current total is not established and any lease-adjusted leverage cannot be built. Closing the gap needs the lease note of the fiscal 2026 annual report. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 93; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation K18

Last-twelve-months EBITDA excludes Breeze Autocare before December 1, 2025 (Medium). No pro forma EBITDA for the acquisition is printed, so leverage at June 30, 2026 is stated on earnings that include the acquired business for seven months of the twelve and the debt that funded it in full. The ratio overstates leverage against a full-year basis by an amount that is not established. Closing the gap needs a pro forma EBITDA from the issuer. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9, 26

Adjusted EBITDA key items are defined differently across periods (Medium). The fiscal 2026 key items include amortization of Breeze acquired intangibles and temporary financing costs, and the information technology label now includes control remediation costs; the last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA of USD 543.5 million mixes the two definitions and the effect is not quantified in the filings. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 51–53; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 26–27; calculation K8

Covenant definitions are not supplied (Medium). The financial covenants are summarised in the fiscal 2025 annual report as a maximum net leverage ratio of 4.5x and a minimum interest coverage ratio of 3.0x, tested each quarter, and the company states compliance at June 30, 2026. The covenant definitions of net debt and Adjusted EBITDA are not supplied, so covenant headroom is not inferred or calculated here. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 97; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 29

Security, rank, margins and floors for the loans are partly not stated (Medium). The security and legal rank of the Term Loan B are taken from the Senior Credit Agreement it amends as Analyst Judgement, because no filing after the amendment restates them. The margins in force at June 30, 2026 for the Term Loan A and the revolver, and any floors, are not stated. The debt stack therefore ranks the three facilities equally. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 96–97; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 12

Interim cash flow lines and dash entries are not supplied (Low). The interim statements do not print deferred income taxes, pension remeasurement, purchases and proceeds of investments, finance lease payments or income taxes paid, so those cells are not supplied for the nine-month columns. Entries printed as a dash are not read as zero: the loss on extinguishment of debt in fiscal 2025, operating cash flows from discontinued operations and repurchases of common stock in the nine months to June 30, 2026, and the exchange effect on cash in fiscal 2024. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 69–70; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4

Total liabilities and the 2025-06-30 balance sheet are not printed (Low). The balance sheets print no total liabilities line, so it is calculated and shown as such, and the June 2026 report prints no balance sheet at June 30, 2025, so net debt at that date and a prior-year last-twelve-months leverage are not available. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 69; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; calculation K4

No segment revenue schedule applies (Low). The issuer reports one segment, so no segment revenue or elimination rows exist and no segment sum is stated; revenue by service category is printed in the quarterly report but is not a segment schedule. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16

Some period-end store counts and event amounts are not printed (Low). Company-operated and franchised store counts for fiscal 2024 are not printed in the text of the fiscal 2024 report. The proceeds of the October 2025 sale of 10 stores are not stated, so the post-balance-sheet table leaves that row unquantified, and the dates of the 21 other store acquisitions are given only as the nine months to June 30, 2026. Basis: 10-K_2024-09-30_vvv-20240930.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 108; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11

Fiscal 2024 comparatives were re-presented (Low). The fiscal 2025 annual report splits fiscal 2024 investing and financing lines more finely than the fiscal 2024 annual report; totals and closing cash are unchanged, and the quarterly reports state that certain prior period amounts were reclassified. Fiscal 2024 figures here follow the later report. Basis: 10-K_2024-09-30_vvv-20240930.htm.jsonl, page 70; 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 70; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 5

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The business is a durable, low-ticket maintenance service. Oil changes and related fees were 73.60% of nine-month revenue, other maintenance services 21.26% and franchise fees 5.14%, and system-wide same-store sales grew 8.0% in the third quarter of fiscal 2026 after 19 consecutive years of growth through fiscal 2025, so demand follows vehicle maintenance needs rather than discretionary spending. Management characterises the network's record as operational excellence; the figures show growth, not the reason for it. Basis: calculation M1; 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16, 22

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Growth now leans heavily on a debt-funded acquisition. Breeze Autocare closed on December 1, 2025 for USD 637.4 million of cash, funded by a USD 740.0 million Term Loan B, and contributed 7.75% of nine-month revenue; the required sale of 45 acquired stores cost a USD 57.9 million pre-tax loss. The mechanism is higher debt service against earnings that include the acquired stores for only part of the period, which is why creditors should read current leverage together with the Financial foundation. Basis: calculation M5; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 8–11

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Margins are under cost pressure that is not yet labour or materials. Gross margin fell by 1.00 percentage points to 39.46% in the third quarter, and most of the decline sits in other service delivery costs, which rose from 19.68% to 20.62% of revenue while labour and materials ratios were flat; management adds that lubricant costs rose through the quarter and are expected to stay elevated. A pricing lag against a single supplier's costs would hit margin next. Basis: calculation M3; calculation M4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 19, 22–23

facts.label: Key findings

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 19, 37

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Governance evidence is thin and its main risk is control reliability. Management reports a material weakness in internal control that began with the 2024 system implementation and persisted at June 30, 2026, the auditor's opinion on internal control was adverse at both prior year-ends, and the acquired business is excluded from the fiscal 2026 assessment, so the reliability of reported figures depends on remediation that management expects during fiscal 2026. The chief financial officer changed in May 2025. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 31–34; 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 66, 110

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Capital allocation was shareholder-led before the acquisition and is creditor-friendly after it. Share repurchases and dividends totalled USD 1,850.2 million across fiscal 2023 to 2025, after the Global Products sale brought in USD 2,383 million, while management has since paused repurchases, prepaid USD 50.0 million of the Term Loan A and lowered its leverage target. The shift is documented but untested by a fiscal 2026 year-end. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is momentum and deleveraging: same-store sales growth of 8.0% in the third quarter, free cash flow of USD 112.3 million in the nine months, a USD 50.0 million prepayment of the Term Loan A, and a franchised half of the network (49.84% of stores) that adds fee income without store capital. The view would improve if the fiscal 2026 year-end shows net leverage inside management's target range, remediation of the control weakness is declared complete, and no further debt-funded acquisition is announced; it would worsen if a gap opens between lubricant costs and pricing or the supply relationship is disrupted. Basis: calculation M9; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 22, 29, 34

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Leverage is the weakest dimension, and the credit case rests on reducing it. Net debt of USD 1,517.8 million is 2.79x Adjusted EBITDA, 0.29x above management's ceiling of 2.5x, and reported EBITDA gives 3.61x because it carries a USD 57.9 million loss on the forced sale of 45 acquired stores. Net debt is USD 125.0 million below the USD 1,642.8 million pro forma figure after the three quantified events that followed the fiscal 2025 balance sheet, so deleveraging has started; earnings include the acquired business for only seven of the twelve months, so the ratio overstates leverage by an amount the filings do not let us measure. Basis: calculation F6; calculation F15; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 8–11, 26, 30

facts.label: Business model and credit linkage
facts.text: The business model supports cash-flow visibility because revenue comes from low-ticket preventive maintenance tied to vehicle use, but it concentrates that visibility in a single service line. Oil changes and related fees were 73.60% of nine-month revenue, other maintenance services 21.26% and franchise fees 5.14%, and 96.89% of fiscal 2025 revenue came from the United States. Stores are 49.84% franchised, so about half of the network pays fees on its sales without drawing on the issuer's capital; the risk mechanic is that royalties and product margin on franchised stores depend on franchisee sales and financing, which the annual report identifies as a dependency. The credit implication is steady, fee-supported cash flow with a narrow base, and a refinancing story that leans on the record of same-store sales growth. facts.label: Ownership and financial policy
facts.text: Ownership is dispersed and no sponsor or controlling shareholder is named, so the credit risk is the willingness of management, not an owner's extraction. The company paid no dividend in fiscal 2024 or fiscal 2025 and does not expect to, but returned USD 1,850.2 million through repurchases and dividends across fiscal 2023 to 2025 after the Global Products sale, and then used a USD 740.0 million Term Loan B to fund a USD 637.4 million acquisition. The mechanic is that policy has moved from returning capital to adding debt for growth; the implication is that creditors should treat the paused repurchases and the lowered range of 1.5x to 2.5x as a commitment still to be proven, because USD 325.0 million of authorization remains and the resumption conditions are not set out. Guarantees of leases and franchisee debt add USD 105.8 million outside reported debt. Basis: calculation F13; calculation F14; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 13, 29–30

facts.label: Revenue durability and pricing power
facts.text: Revenue is recurring and mostly non-discretionary, but pricing power is untested at the margin. Net revenues grew 5.64% in fiscal 2025, 20.19% in the first nine months of fiscal 2026 and 24.05% in the third quarter, where USD 50.8 million of the USD 105.6 million increase came from the acquired business, while system-wide same-store sales grew 8.0% with higher volumes and favourable pricing and service mix. The mechanic is that a customer can defer an oil change in a downturn or as miles driven fall, which the annual report lists as a risk, so durability rests on the company's ability to hold volume as prices rise. The implication is that revenue is predictable in normal conditions and cyclical at the margin, with no customer concentration measured. facts.label: Cost structure and margin resilience
facts.text: Margin resilience rests on pass-through to franchisees and pricing action in company-operated stores, against a cost base of labour, materials and other service delivery costs. Labour was 24.29% of revenue and materials 17.39% in fiscal 2025, and in the third quarter of fiscal 2026 other service delivery costs rose to 20.62% of revenue from 19.68% while labour and materials were flat. The mechanic is operating leverage on store labour and a supplier whose prices follow base oil; the implication is that a sustained cost squeeze would reach Adjusted EBITDA before it reaches liquidity, and that wage legislation or tariffs, which the annual report flags, would add to it. facts.label: Competitive forces
facts.text: Rivalry is the force that matters most for margin: the market is fragmented and Valvoline competes with dealerships, repair centers and other quick-lube chains on brand, price, speed and location, so it can pass on cost but not earn above-cost pricing everywhere. Buyer power appears high because the filings show no switching cost for a consumer and give no measure of fleet or franchisee concentration; the largest franchisees add concentration risk to the royalty stream. Supplier power is high: substantially all lubricants come from one counterparty under a long-term agreement whose terms are not supplied. Substitutes are limited today, but electric vehicles and longer drain intervals, and owners who maintain their own vehicles, reduce visits over time. New entrants face the cost of real estate and brand building, which limits their effect on credit within the horizon. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8, 17–18, 20, 23, 25

facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The realistic downside is a cost and demand squeeze that starts in company-operated store margin and ends in a refinancing at higher leverage. The initiating condition is that lubricant costs, which management expects to stay elevated, rise faster than prices at the same time as an economic slowdown or higher energy prices lead customers to defer oil changes. The first operational break is gross margin: the fall of 1.00 percentage points already seen in the third quarter of fiscal 2026 is worth USD 19.64 million of Adjusted EBITDA over a year of revenue, and fewer vehicles served per day would add to it through operating leverage on store labour. The financial transmission is arithmetic on net debt of USD 1,517.8 million: a 10% fall in Adjusted EBITDA lifts net leverage from 2.79x to 3.10x and a 20% fall to 3.49x, expense-based cover falls from 5.32x to 4.79x and 4.26x, and free cash flow before any tax relief falls from USD 140.5 million to USD 86.15 million and USD 31.80 million, still positive before any cut in growth spending. Basis: calculation F7; calculation F4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 19

The first operational break is gross margin: the fall of 1.00 percentage points already seen in the third quarter of fiscal 2026 is worth USD 19.64 million of Adjusted EBITDA over a year of revenue, and fewer vehicles served per day would add to it through operating leverage on store labour. The financial transmission is arithmetic on net debt of USD 1,517.8 million: a 10% fall in Adjusted EBITDA lifts net leverage from 2.79x to 3.10x and a 20% fall to 3.49x, expense-based cover falls from 5.32x to 4.79x and 4.26x, and free cash flow before any tax relief falls from USD 140.5 million to USD 86.15 million and USD 31.80 million, still positive before any cut in growth spending.
Basis: calculation F7; calculation F4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 19

facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: Liquidity holds under this path: USD 554.3 million of liquidity compares with USD 47.6 million of installments printed for fiscal 2026 and fiscal 2027 and an undrawn revolver. The consequence arrives at refinancing, where the fiscal 2028 bucket and the revolver would be refinanced at leverage nearer 3.5x than the ceiling of 2.5x, with 67.00% of principal floating, so a rise in base rates of 1.00 percentage points adds USD 10.86 million of annual interest. Management's levers are to defer the USD 129.0 million of nine-month growth spending, keep repurchases paused, slow acquisitions and refranchise stores. They appear sufficient to avoid a liquidity shortfall over the next 12 months to 24 months but not to return leverage to the range without a recovery in earnings. The observable triggers are gross margin below 39.46% in consecutive quarters, same-store sales growth turning negative and net leverage rising above 2.79x. The sensitivities are Analyst Judgement arithmetic, not forecasts, and the covenant tests cannot be applied because their definitions are not supplied. Basis: calculation F5; calculation F7; calculation F8; calculation F10; 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 97; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 29–30

facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Valvoline presents an adequate business profile supported by recurring maintenance demand, a franchised half of the network and deferrable growth capital expenditure, but credit quality is constrained by net leverage of 2.79x above management's ceiling of 2.5x, concentration in one service line, one country and one supplier, and a continuing control weakness. Cash-flow durability appears adequate due to an Adjusted EBITDA margin of 27.67% that has been stable across three periods and free cash flow of USD 140.5 million over the last twelve months, which is thin against net debt at 10.80x. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the maturity dates of the revolver and term loans, on the control remediation and on whether leverage reaches the ceiling before the fiscal 2028 bucket falls due. The primary downside path is a lubricant cost squeeze or a demand slowdown that raises leverage toward 3.5x with two-thirds of the debt floating. Basis: calculation F1; calculation F4; calculation F6; calculation F7; calculation F8

## Request

Source readiness for Valvoline Inc (issuer vvv-1674910), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: whether the five supplied filings can support the requested Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit analyses, and what is missing.

No upstream analytical handoff was supplied; Source readiness is the first module of this run.
## Findings
### Bottom line

The five Valvoline filings support a credit snapshot as at June 30, 2026, not later: debt, cash and revolver availability are usable, but covenant headroom and the maturity schedule after the 2025 term loan are not. The latest balance sheet is 141 days before the as-of date, and the fiscal 2026 annual report, executed credit documents, ratings, market prices and peer data are absent. Covenant levels (maximum net leverage 4.5x, minimum interest coverage 3.0x) come only from the fiscal 2025 annual report's summary, so management's statement of compliance at June 30, 2026 cannot be tested.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 29; 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 97; calculation C1

A material weakness in financial-reporting controls persisted at June 30, 2026 and the auditor's opinions on internal control were adverse at both prior year-ends, so the unaudited quarterly figures carry added reliability risk, although management reports no identified material misstatement. Management's leverage target also moved without explanation, from 2.5x to 3.5x in the December 2025 report to 1.5x to 2.5x in the March 2026 report. Otherwise the filings suffice for the three requested analyses, each within the limits stated here.

**No filing after June 30, 2026 (material).** The latest supplied report covers the quarter ended June 30, 2026 and was signed on August 5, 2026. The fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2024 annual reports were signed 52 days and 53 days after their year-ends, so it is not established whether a fiscal 2026 annual report exists at the as-of date. Year-end debt, cash, covenant compliance and fourth-quarter results are therefore not available, and every balance quoted for Valvoline is at June 30, 2026 or earlier.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 32, 35; 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 120; 10-K_2024-09-30_vvv-20240930.htm.jsonl, page 123; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4

The quarterly statements are unaudited, and the acquired Breeze business, about 8% of nine-month net revenues and about 20% of total assets, is excluded from management's fiscal 2026 assessment. Figures from these filings are usable but carry a reliability qualification until remediation is shown.

**Maturity schedule and lease balances after the 2025 amendments not printed (minor).** The latest debt maturity table is at September 30, 2025, before the Term Loan B: USD 23.8 million in fiscal 2026, USD 23.8 million in fiscal 2027, USD 498.0 million in fiscal 2028 and USD 535.0 million thereafter. The quarterly reports print no maturity table and do not state the maturity dates of the Term Loan B (a seven-year facility), the Term Loan A or the revolver, so the maturity wall at June 30, 2026 is not established. Finance lease liabilities, which sit outside total debt, were USD 244.5 million at September 30, 2025 and are not printed for June 30, 2026. No supplied filing mentions purchase commitments, factoring or supplier finance.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 93, 97; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 12; calculation C8; calculation C9

**Ratings, market data, peers and outlook not supplied (minor).** No credit rating, rating-agency comment, bond or loan price, spread, peer set, earnings release or call transcript is supplied, and the run settings carry none. A search of all five filings for rating-agency names and for guidance or outlook found no numerical earnings or cash flow guidance beyond a fiscal 2026 capital expenditure forecast of USD 250 million to USD 280 million in the fiscal 2025 annual report. The June 2026 report says share repurchases resume on achievement of commitments established at the time of the acquisition, but no supplied document sets those commitments out. The only market-based figure for the debt is the fair value of the 2031 Notes, USD 492.6 million at June 30, 2026 against a carrying value of USD 531.5 million.

**Board, ownership and compensation not supplied (minor).** Directors, executive compensation, beneficial ownership and related-party information are incorporated by reference from a proxy statement that is not supplied. The fiscal 2025 annual report lists the executive officers as of November 18, 2025. The run settings name no sponsor, parent or guarantor, so ownership and governance beyond the officer list are not established.

**Differing figures and targets between reports (minor).** The pre-tax gain on the sale of 10 company-operated stores to a franchisee in the first quarter of fiscal 2026 is USD 14.8 million in the quarter to December 31, 2025 and in the six months to March 31, 2026, but USD 14.3 million in the nine months to June 30, 2026, a difference of USD 0.5 million. The prior-year gain on the 39-store sale moves from USD 73.9 million to USD 74.2 million to USD 74.3 million over the same three reports. Separately, the fiscal 2025 annual report expected the Breeze acquisition to cover 207 stores for a net purchase price of USD 593 million, subject to adjustments, while the June 2026 report gives cash consideration of USD 637.4 million and says the acquisition initially included 204 stores; neither report reconciles the two. Management's leverage target also changes: both annual reports and the December 2025 quarterly report describe a ratings agency target adjusted EBITDA net leverage ratio of 2.5x to 3.5x, while the March and June 2026 quarterly reports give a net debt to Adjusted EBITDA ratio of 1.5x to 2.5x, so the two targets are not on one stated definition. No filing explains these changes. The quarterly reports also state that certain prior period amounts were reclassified, so prior-year comparatives may differ from the original fiscal 2025 annual report. The June 2026 figures are the latest and are used as the current reading.

### Leverage and coverage

Reported total debt to EBITDA fell from 2.37x at fiscal 2024 year-end to 2.21x at fiscal 2025 year-end, then rose to 3.81x on last-twelve-months EBITDA at June 30, 2026 as the Term Loan B funded the Breeze Autocare acquisition and carrying-value debt rose from USD 1,074.0 million to USD 1,602.0 million. Reported EBITDA overstates the rise in leverage: the nine months to June 30, 2026 carry a USD 57.9 million pre-tax loss on the required sale of 45 acquired stores, and Breeze Autocare contributes only from December 1, 2025. On issuer Adjusted EBITDA the same ratio is 2.95x, against 2.30x at fiscal 2025 year-end.
Basis: calculation K5; calculation K7; calculation K8; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11, 26

Net debt to Adjusted EBITDA of 2.79x at June 30, 2026 is 0.29x above the top of management's stated range of 1.5x to 2.5x. Management lowered that range from 2.5x to 3.5x between the December 2025 and March 2026 reports and no supplied report explains the change; it says it has made substantial progress and paused repurchases to deleverage, but the supplied figures show the range has not yet been reached.
Basis: calculation K19; 10-Q_2025-12-31_vvv-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-03-31_vvv-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 30

Cash interest cover rose from 5.90x in fiscal 2024 to 8.66x in fiscal 2025 as interest paid fell from USD 78.2 million to USD 56.1 million after the 2030 notes were retired. That cover pre-dates the Term Loan B: net interest and other financing expenses were USD 81.1 million in the nine months to June 30, 2026 against USD 53.0 million, and last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA covers that expense 5.32x, an expense-based measure that is not the covenant test. Cash interest cover on the current debt load is not calculable because the quarterly reports print no interest paid.
Basis: calculation K14; 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 54, 70; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2

The strongest contrary evidence is cash generation. Free cash flow was USD 112.3 million in the nine months to June 30, 2026 against USD 19.7 million a year earlier, and USD 50.0 million of the Term Loan A was prepaid in the quarter. It would carry more weight if fiscal 2026 year-end figures show net debt below USD 1,517.8 million without further acquisitions, and it carries less weight because the other assets and liabilities line turned from an outflow of USD 0.2 million to an inflow of USD 42.6 million.
Basis: calculation K3; calculation K13; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 12, 28
### Cash flow quality

Operating cash flow from continuing operations was USD 284.6 million in the nine months to June 30, 2026 against USD 180.0 million a year earlier, an increase of USD 104.6 million of which the issuer attributes USD 80.4 million to higher cash earnings and, to a lesser extent, lower cloud computing implementation spend. Payables and accrued liabilities swung from an outflow of USD 28.4 million to an outflow of USD 0.7 million, so part of the improvement may be working-capital timing.
Basis: calculation K23; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 28

Free cash flow converts 33.41% of last-twelve-months reported EBITDA, against 9.86% in fiscal 2025, because the operating inflow rose while capital expenditure stayed at 13.81% of last-twelve-months revenue. Maintenance capital expenditure was USD 43.3 million in the nine months against USD 35.1 million, and growth capital expenditure USD 129.0 million against USD 125.2 million, so most of the spend is growth capital expenditure.
Basis: calculation K13; calculation K15; calculation K24; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 29
### Liquidity and maturities

Liquidity at June 30, 2026 was USD 554.3 million: cash of USD 84.2 million and USD 470.1 million undrawn on the USD 475.0 million revolver after USD 4.9 million of letters of credit, against USD 393.2 million at fiscal 2025 year-end. The last printed maturity ladder, at September 30, 2025, shows USD 23.8 million due in each of fiscal 2026 and fiscal 2027, USD 498.0 million in fiscal 2028 and USD 535.0 million thereafter. It predates the USD 740.0 million Term Loan B, whose seven-year maturity date is not printed, so the maturity wall at June 30, 2026 is not established.
Basis: calculation K16; calculation K10; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 96–97

About 33% of borrowings at June 30, 2026 had fixed rates, against approximately 50% at September 30, 2025, and the June 30, 2026 repricing cut the Term Loan B margin by 0.25 percentage points; the floating-rate share therefore leaves interest cost sensitive to base rates.
### Data quality and definition risks

Every figure rests on filings with a continuing material weakness in financial-reporting controls, and the quarterly statements are unaudited, although management reports no identified material misstatement. The statements nevertheless tie internally: assets equal liabilities plus equity at all three balance sheet dates, the cash flow totals reconcile to the change in cash in every column, and EBITDA rebuilds from its components in every column.
Basis: calculation K6; calculation K21; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 31–34

Claims outside the debt figure include finance lease liabilities of USD 244.5 million at fiscal 2025 year-end, noncurrent operating lease liabilities of USD 377.3 million and employee benefit obligations of USD 178.9 million at June 30, 2026, lease guarantees of USD 93.4 million and franchisee debt guarantees of USD 12.4 million. None is in total debt, and the finance lease total at June 30, 2026 is not established.
Basis: calculation K18; 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 93; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 13
No non-debt funding float is material: the issuer states that contract liabilities are not material, and no filing mentions supplier finance or factoring.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 73, 80

Subsequent events are dated and kept out of period figures. The Breeze Autocare acquisition closed on December 1, 2025, with 45 stores sold the same day; the pro forma effect on fiscal 2025 year-end net debt is in the post-balance-sheet table, with the sale of 10 stores to a franchisee left unquantified because no proceeds are stated. The gain on that sale is USD 14.8 million in two reports and USD 14.3 million in the third, a difference of USD 0.5 million that no filing explains.
Basis: calculation K17; calculation K22; 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 108; 10-Q_2025-12-31_vvv-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 9–11

**Interim cash interest paid is not printed (High).** The nine-month cash flow statements print no interest paid, so Cash Interest Paid is not supplied for the nine months to June 30, 2026 and the nine months to June 30, 2025. EBITDA to cash interest at June 30, 2026 is therefore not calculable, and the interest cover charts stop at fiscal 2025 year-end, before the Term Loan B raised debt. Closing the gap needs interest paid for the twelve months to June 30, 2026 or the fiscal 2026 annual report.

**No statements after June 30, 2026 (High).** Every balance and the last-twelve-months construction end at June 30, 2026. Year-end fiscal 2026 debt, cash, EBITDA and cash interest are not available, and the pro forma table covers only events after the fiscal 2025 balance sheet. Closing the gap needs the fiscal 2026 annual report.

**Maturity dates and the maturity wall after the Term Loan B are not printed (Medium).** The only maturity ladder is at September 30, 2025, with fiscal 2029 and fiscal 2030 printed as dashes that the printed total shows to be nil. No report prints the maturity date of the Term Loan A, the Term Loan B or the revolver, or a ladder after the December 2025 amendment, so the maturity wall at June 30, 2026 is not established and the fiscal 2031 bucket is placed by Analyst Judgement. Closing the gap needs the executed credit agreement and its amendments.

**Carrying values by instrument are not printed (Medium).** Only the 2031 Notes' carrying value is printed, so the Term Loan A and Term Loan B carry principal in the instrument register and the remaining issuance costs and discounts of USD 15.5 million are one adjustment row. **Finance lease liabilities at June 30, 2026 are not printed (Medium).** Finance lease liabilities were USD 244.5 million at September 30, 2025 and sit outside total debt; the June 2026 report prints only the amounts assumed with Breeze Autocare, so the current total is not established and any lease-adjusted leverage cannot be built. Closing the gap needs the lease note of the fiscal 2026 annual report.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 93; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation K18

**Last-twelve-months EBITDA excludes Breeze Autocare before December 1, 2025 (Medium).** No pro forma EBITDA for the acquisition is printed, so leverage at June 30, 2026 is stated on earnings that include the acquired business for seven months of the twelve and the debt that funded it in full. The ratio overstates leverage against a full-year basis by an amount that is not established. Closing the gap needs a pro forma EBITDA from the issuer.

**Adjusted EBITDA key items are defined differently across periods (Medium).** The fiscal 2026 key items include amortization of Breeze acquired intangibles and temporary financing costs, and the information technology label now includes control remediation costs; the last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA of USD 543.5 million mixes the two definitions and the effect is not quantified in the filings.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 51–53; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 26–27; calculation K8

**Covenant definitions are not supplied (Medium).** The financial covenants are summarised in the fiscal 2025 annual report as a maximum net leverage ratio of 4.5x and a minimum interest coverage ratio of 3.0x, tested each quarter, and the company states compliance at June 30, 2026. The covenant definitions of net debt and Adjusted EBITDA are not supplied, so covenant headroom is not inferred or calculated here.

**Security, rank, margins and floors for the loans are partly not stated (Medium).** The security and legal rank of the Term Loan B are taken from the Senior Credit Agreement it amends as Analyst Judgement, because no filing after the amendment restates them. The margins in force at June 30, 2026 for the Term Loan A and the revolver, and any floors, are not stated. The debt stack therefore ranks the three facilities equally.

**Interim cash flow lines and dash entries are not supplied (Low).** The interim statements do not print deferred income taxes, pension remeasurement, purchases and proceeds of investments, finance lease payments or income taxes paid, so those cells are not supplied for the nine-month columns. Entries printed as a dash are not read as zero: the loss on extinguishment of debt in fiscal 2025, operating cash flows from discontinued operations and repurchases of common stock in the nine months to June 30, 2026, and the exchange effect on cash in fiscal 2024.

**Total liabilities and the 2025-06-30 balance sheet are not printed (Low).** The balance sheets print no total liabilities line, so it is calculated and shown as such, and the June 2026 report prints no balance sheet at June 30, 2025, so net debt at that date and a prior-year last-twelve-months leverage are not available.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 69; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; calculation K4

**No segment revenue schedule applies (Low).** The issuer reports one segment, so no segment revenue or elimination rows exist and no segment sum is stated; revenue by service category is printed in the quarterly report but is not a segment schedule.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16

**Some period-end store counts and event amounts are not printed (Low).** Company-operated and franchised store counts for fiscal 2024 are not printed in the text of the fiscal 2024 report. The proceeds of the October 2025 sale of 10 stores are not stated, so the post-balance-sheet table leaves that row unquantified, and the dates of the 21 other store acquisitions are given only as the nine months to June 30, 2026.

**Fiscal 2024 comparatives were re-presented (Low).** The fiscal 2025 annual report splits fiscal 2024 investing and financing lines more finely than the fiscal 2024 annual report; totals and closing cash are unchanged, and the quarterly reports state that certain prior period amounts were reclassified. Fiscal 2024 figures here follow the later report.

spans.text: # Business & governance: Valvoline Inc (vvv-1674910), as of 2026-11-18
## Request

Business & governance for Valvoline Inc (issuer vvv-1674910), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the business, operating model, ownership, transactions, governance and capital allocation from the five supplied filings, with every gap stated.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2024-09-30_vvv-20240930.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended September 30, 2024 | 2024-11-22 (date signed; filing date not stated) | 24690964c18f2016719f4c7f7a46038637a00e91394e9c843c24fae37d5f50cc | Proceeds of the Global Products sale, fiscal 2023 and 2024 share repurchases, store count and same-store sales for fiscal 2024 |

| 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended September 30, 2025 | 2025-11-21 (date signed; filing date not stated) | b885defac1ff52441e2e04ee4701c7fcdae244ad16d0fbad6ac620fc6c84dd6d | Business description, strategy, supply agreement, executive officers, ownership and Part III references, risk factors, revenue and cost mix, capital allocation, subsequent events |

| 10-Q_2025-12-31_vvv-20251231.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended December 31, 2025 | 2026-02-04 (date signed; filing date not stated) | a98fe86113b9a801f93408e3fac808cb3311459a0eb335f86b700a37071004c6 | First report of the Breeze Autocare acquisition, the Term Loan B and the sale of 10 stores; the earlier leverage target wording |

| 10-Q_2026-03-31_vvv-20260331.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2026 | 2026-05-07 (date signed; filing date not stated) | dbbb3a3f2ca063cbd68b6c914b0b96c7cbb76fca745940506fb80508df967e2b | Revised leverage target wording and the store-sale gain as restated |

| 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 | 2026-08-05 (date signed; filing date not stated) | 17f9c0c8aa70e246edd10d76211ff714f7b95c7bbe84af1d2f45ed0381b5daca | Breeze Autocare closing and contribution, store counts, margins, cost mix, lubricant cost commentary, repricing, controls and remediation |
| Handoff | Module | sha256 | Use |
| Source readiness | CP-0 | 3c1213c3887eb0aa5a9baf90f63cbd23435441fe6d32de76ea76913ccb897442 | Source coverage, absent documents and the differing figures between reports |
## Findings
### Bottom line

Valvoline's operating model is resilient, but creditors now hold claims on an acquisitive, more leveraged issuer: nineteen years of same-store sales growth support cash flow, while a debt-funded acquisition, reliance on one lubricant supplier and a continuing control weakness add event and reporting risk.

Nearly half of third-quarter revenue growth came from the acquisition: Breeze Autocare added USD 50.8 million of the USD 105.6 million increase. No sponsor or controlling shareholder is named in the supplied filings and the company pays no dividend and does not expect to, which limits extraction risk, but board and ownership detail is not established.
Basis: calculation M7; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 22; 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 42, 70, 114–115
### Key findings

The business is a durable, low-ticket maintenance service. Oil changes and related fees were 73.60% of nine-month revenue, other maintenance services 21.26% and franchise fees 5.14%, and system-wide same-store sales grew 8.0% in the third quarter of fiscal 2026 after 19 consecutive years of growth through fiscal 2025, so demand follows vehicle maintenance needs rather than discretionary spending. Management characterises the network's record as operational excellence; the figures show growth, not the reason for it.
Basis: calculation M1; 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16, 22

Growth now leans heavily on a debt-funded acquisition. Breeze Autocare closed on December 1, 2025 for USD 637.4 million of cash, funded by a USD 740.0 million Term Loan B, and contributed 7.75% of nine-month revenue; the required sale of 45 acquired stores cost a USD 57.9 million pre-tax loss. The mechanism is higher debt service against earnings that include the acquired stores for only part of the period, which is why creditors should read current leverage together with the Financial foundation.
Basis: calculation M5; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 8–11

Margins are under cost pressure that is not yet labour or materials. Gross margin fell by 1.00 percentage points to 39.46% in the third quarter, and most of the decline sits in other service delivery costs, which rose from 19.68% to 20.62% of revenue while labour and materials ratios were flat; management adds that lubricant costs rose through the quarter and are expected to stay elevated. A pricing lag against a single supplier's costs would hit margin next.
Basis: calculation M3; calculation M4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 19, 22–23

Supply is concentrated in one counterparty. The stores buy substantially all lubricants from the owner of the former Global Products business under a long-term supply agreement, and the brand is shared with that owner; any interruption, quality failure or dispute would reach every company-operated store and the franchisees' product supply at once.

Governance evidence is thin and its main risk is control reliability. Management reports a material weakness in internal control that began with the 2024 system implementation and persisted at June 30, 2026, the auditor's opinion on internal control was adverse at both prior year-ends, and the acquired business is excluded from the fiscal 2026 assessment, so the reliability of reported figures depends on remediation that management expects during fiscal 2026. The chief financial officer changed in May 2025.

Capital allocation was shareholder-led before the acquisition and is creditor-friendly after it. Share repurchases and dividends totalled USD 1,850.2 million across fiscal 2023 to 2025, after the Global Products sale brought in USD 2,383 million, while management has since paused repurchases, prepaid USD 50.0 million of the Term Loan A and lowered its leverage target. The shift is documented but untested by a fiscal 2026 year-end.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a cautious view is momentum and deleveraging: same-store sales growth of 8.0% in the third quarter, free cash flow of USD 112.3 million in the nine months, a USD 50.0 million prepayment of the Term Loan A, and a franchised half of the network (49.84% of stores) that adds fee income without store capital. The view would improve if the fiscal 2026 year-end shows net leverage inside management's target range, remediation of the control weakness is declared complete, and no further debt-funded acquisition is announced; it would worsen if a gap opens between lubricant costs and pricing or the supply relationship is disrupted.
Basis: calculation M9; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 22, 29, 34
### Limitations

- Directors, compensation and shareholder detail sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied, so the governance view rests on officers and filings and could move to lower risk if the proxy shows independent oversight of the control remediation.
- The supply agreement's term, pricing and minimum purchase terms are not supplied, so the supplier concentration cannot be sized; terms that favour the supplier would raise the risk.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 37
- The earnings contribution of Breeze Autocare is not stated, only its revenue and net income, so the acquisition's effect on cash flow and on leverage is not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 9
- No customer or franchisee concentration data is supplied, so the durability finding rests on the breadth of a consumer and commercial customer base that the filings describe but do not measure.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 5
### Company and operating model
| Item | Detail | Source |

| What it does | Quick, easy preventive maintenance for cars: stay-in-the-car oil changes of about 15 minutes, battery, bulb, wiper and tire rotation services, through company-operated and franchised service centers | 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5 |

| Network | System-wide stores 2,456 at 2026-06-30, of which 1,232 company-operated and 1,224 franchised; 2,124 a year earlier; the Express Care platform supports over 240 further locations | 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 22 |

| Revenue model | Net revenues come from company-operated store sales and from royalties and fees from franchised and Express Care stores; nine months to 2026-06-30: oil changes and related fees 73.60%, non-oil changes and related fees 21.26%, franchise fees and other 5.14% | 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16, 22 |

| Customers and geography | Consumers and commercial customers; revenue is almost entirely in the United States (96.89% of fiscal 2025 revenue) with Canada the only other market; no customer concentration is stated | 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 81 |

| Competitive position | Management describes itself as the trusted leader in automotive preventive maintenance in a fragmented market; competitors include dealerships, repair centers and other franchised brands | 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 6–7 |

| Supply | Substantially all lubricants and certain ancillary products are bought from the owner of the former Global Products business under a long-term supply agreement; product pricing to independent operators follows base oil indices | 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9 |

| Strategy | Drive the core business, grow the network through company-operated stores and franchisee stores, and expand fleet and non-oil services; company-operated stores increased by acquisition and development | 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 17 |
| Seasonality | Moderate; the second half of the fiscal year is ordinarily stronger because miles driven are higher | 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 9 |

| Cost structure | Fiscal 2025: labour 24.29% and materials 17.39% of revenue, other service delivery and corporate costs the rest; third quarter of fiscal 2026 cost of sales is 60.54% of revenue | 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 106; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 15 |
### Company profile
| Item | Detail | Source |

| Issuer | Valvoline Inc, a Kentucky corporation headquartered in Lexington, Kentucky; commission file number 001-37884 | 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 42 |

| Listing and holders | Common stock listed on the New York Stock Exchange as VVV; 127,586,418 shares outstanding at 2026-07-30; about 7,060 registered holders at 2025-11-18 | 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 42 |

| Controlling shareholder or sponsor | Not supplied: none is named in the supplied filings and beneficial ownership is in a proxy statement that is not supplied | 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 114–115 |
| Fiscal year and auditor | Fiscal year ends September 30; Ernst & Young LLP has audited the company since 2016 | 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 66, 68 |

| Executive officers (as of 2025-11-18) | Chief executive officer since October 2023; chief financial officer since May 2025; chief legal officer since January 2017; chief operating officer since October 2023; chief people officer since April 2020 | 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 15 |
| Employees | About 11,400 at 2025-09-30, of whom about 10,100 work in company-operated stores | 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 10 |
| Reportable segments | One; the chief executive officer reviews consolidated results | 10-Q_2026-06-30_vvv-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 15 |

| Origin | Founded in 1866; owned by Ashland from 1950; incorporated as an Ashland subsidiary in May 2016, listed in September 2016 and distributed by Ashland in May 2017 | 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5 |
| Ratings | Not supplied: no credit rating appears in the supplied filings or run settings | 10-K_2025-09-30_vvv-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 55 |
### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The transaction that defines the credit today is the acquisition of Breeze Autocare, an independent operator of quick lube stores in California, Texas and the Midwest, signed in February 2025 and closed on December 1, 2025 for USD 637.4 million of cash, with the Federal Trade Commission requiring the immediate sale of 45 acquired stores. The seller named in the annual report is Greenbriar; the buyer of the 45 stores named there is Mainstreet Auto, LLC.

The acquisition was funded by a new seven-year Term Loan B of USD 740.0 million added to the Senior Credit Agreement in December 2025, with the excess used to repay the revolver. On June 30, 2026 the Term Loan B was repriced to the adjusted term Secured Overnight Financing Rate plus 1.750% from 2.000%, and Valvoline prepaid USD 50.0 million of the Term Loan A in the third quarter. The 2031 notes of USD 535.0 million were not changed.

Earlier history shapes the structure: the former Global Products business was sold to Aramco Overseas Company B.V. on March 1, 2023 for net proceeds of USD 2,383 million, leaving a supply agreement, a shared brand agreement and indemnities with the buyer's business and with Ashland.
### Events: Issuer history
